Giovanni Boccaccio, The Decameron, translated by John Payne.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/giovanni-boccaccio/the-decameron/john-payne

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Giovanni Boccaccio, the author, the annotator and the writer of the preface, died 1375.
- John Payne, the translator, died 1916.

First publication of the text used: 1886 (SE colophon: 'The Decameron was written from 1348–1353 by Giovanni Boccaccio. It was translated from Italian in 1886 by John Payne.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1886, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain. Standard Ebooks also states this in its rights statement below.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name the country of first publication, and every person whose words are in the text died by 1925, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last to die, John Payne, died 1916; life + 100 years ended in 2016, so the text is public domain there from 1 January 2017.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
